title: Component module adjunction unit on extremally disconnected tests
statement: Let W be an affine scheme whose global ring is w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal], and let S be its profinite space of components [def-zl-generic-component-data]. Let A be any ring sheaf on the coherent profinite slice over S, and B a ring sheaf on the small pro-etale site of W [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let L be a left adjoint to component ring pushforward, adj its adjunction and c:L(A) ≅ B an isomorphism. Put a=adj.unit(A) followed by pushforward(c). Assume that the module pushforward along a admits a left adjoint, and use Mathlib's chosen module pullback adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. For any extremally disconnected profinite E over S and any sheaf of A-modules M [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the component at E of the module adjunction unit M → pushforward(pullback(M)) is a bijective function. Ring and module values lie in universe u+1 and schemes and profinite spaces in universe u. Empty W and empty E are included.

source.place: Proposition 4.3(1), proof of the unit equivalence by extremally disconnected tests and w-contractibility of X times over pi_0(X) E; Bhatt–Scholze Lemmas 2.2.8, 2.4.8.

proof.text: Apply the affine component-site theorem to $W$: $W_E$ is affine ind-etale over $W$, its underlying ringed space is $|W|\times_S E$ with the inverse-image structure sheaf, and $\pi_0(W_E)=E$. In particular its local-ring maps from $W$ are isomorphisms. The w-local component theorem identifies $W^c$ homeomorphically with $S$ and gives the unique closed specialization $c(w)$ of each $w$. In the pullback space $(w,e)$ specializes to $(c(w),e)$: specialization is coordinatewise in a product and restricts to a subspace. The latter point is closed, since both its coordinates are closed. Conversely every closed point must equal this specialization. Thus $(W_E)^c=W^c\times_S E$, a closed subset, and every point has exactly one closed specialization. The local ring at $(c,e)$ is that at $c$ in $W$, hence strictly henselian. Since $E$ is extremally disconnected, the definition now gives that $W_E$ is w-contractible.

source.place: Proposition 4.3(1), proof: the paragraph beginning "As X times over pi_0 X S"; BS Lemmas 2.1.4, 2.2.8, 2.4.8

proof.text: Check the precise split-cover hypothesis of the inverse-image evaluation theorem. For a finite qcqs pro-etale cover $\{V_i\to W_E\}$, the w-contractible clopen-partition theorem gives a finite disjoint clopen partition $W_E=\coprod_k U_k$ and $W_E$-maps $U_k\to V_{i_k}$. Compose each map with the relevant coproduct inclusion into $\coprod_i V_i$. These maps glue on the disjoint open partition to a scheme map $\sigma:W_E\to\coprod_iV_i$. Its composite to $W_E$ restricts to the identity on each $U_k$, hence is the identity. The qcqs finite coproduct exists by the cited coproduct theorem. This proves the required split-cover condition, without assuming that a connected component or a singleton member of the original cover admits a lift. The component evaluation theorem therefore gives $(\pi_W^{-1}A)(W_E)=A(E)$ naturally for set, abelian-group and ring sheaves $A$.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.13(1), with Stacks Tag 098F, lemma-w-contractible-proetale-cover, for the split-cover input

proof.text: Pin down this canonical identification against the adjunction. Write $a(D)=W_D$. A $W$-map $W_E\to W_D$ determines a continuous map to $D$, which factors uniquely through $\pi_0(W_E)=E$ since $D$ is totally disconnected. Conversely a map $h:E\to D$ over $S$ gives the continuous map $(w,e)\mapsto(w,h(e))$ to $W_D$; the stalk-isomorphism lifting theorem gives its unique scheme lift over $W$. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_W(W_E,W_D)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(E,D)$. In the indexing category of pairs $(D,\phi:W_E\to W_D)$, $(E,\operatorname{id})$ is initial, hence terminal after taking opposites. The left Kan colimit is therefore $A(E)$, with the coprojection of $(E,\operatorname{id})$ the identity under this identification. The sheafification comparison at $W_E$ is invertible by the preceding evaluation theorem. The unit of the composite Kan-extension/sheafification adjunction sends $s\in A(E)$ to the sheafification of precisely that identity-index coprojection. Consequently its evaluated map is $s\mapsto s$, not just an unspecified automorphism of $A(E)$.

source.place: Tags 00VE and 00WX, lemma-adjoints-u and lemma-adjoint-sheaves; BS Lemma 2.2.8, more precise right-adjoint formulation

proof.text: The same continuous-site adjunction makes direct image actual restriction: $(G_WN)(E)=N(a(E))=N(W_E)$. Lift inverse image and direct image to modules using geometric module transport. Its normalization says that the underlying transpose is the set-sheaf transpose, so the unit on underlying sheaves is exactly the unit calculated in step 3. The coefficient map is the given isomorphism $\pi_W^{-1}\Lambda_S\cong p_W^*\Lambda$; scalar extension along this isomorphism identifies $p_W^*\Lambda\otimes_{\pi_W^{-1}\Lambda_S}\pi_W^{-1}M$ with $\pi_W^{-1}M$ by $a\otimes m\mapsto am$. Apply step 2 simultaneously to the ring, the module's underlying abelian sheaf and its action. Naturality with respect to the action and product comparisons gives the ordinary $\Lambda_S(E)$-action on $M(E)$. Thus $(G_WF_WM)(E)=M(E)$ as modules and $\eta_M(E)=\operatorname{id}_{M(E)}$. All identifications commute with restriction maps and module morphisms because the colimit coprojections, sheafification and operation comparisons do. Uniqueness of left adjoints transports this unit calculation to Mathlib's chosen module pullback and to any ring left adjoint L with specified coefficient isomorphism c.

source.place: Tags 03D3 and 03D7, lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules and lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules; HRS Proposition 4.3(1)

proof.text: The preceding arguments include the empty cases. If $E=\varnothing$, then the pullback $W_E$ is empty, its component and closed-point spaces are empty, and every local-ring assertion is vacuous. A sheaf of abelian groups or modules takes the empty object to the zero module by the empty-cover sheaf axiom, so the evaluation and unit identities are identities of zero modules. The clopen partition in step 2 may be empty. If $W=\varnothing$, then $S=\varnothing$ and the slice profinite site has only the empty object; both module-sheaf categories are zero categories. The same formulas prove exactness and invertibility of the unit there. All constructions use compatible small sites in the stipulated coefficient universes; Stonean covers may be formed in the ambient Grothendieck universe (closure under power sets), followed by the chosen small-skeleton convention.

lean.statement:
theorem component_module_unit_bijective_on_stonean_tests
    (W : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine W] [IsWContractibleRing Γ(W, ⊤)]
    (A : Sheaf ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).over (componentProfinite W)) RingCat.{u + 1})
    (B : Sheaf (topology W) RingCat.{u + 1})
    (L : Sheaf ((coherentTopology Profinite.{u}).over (componentProfinite W)) RingCat.{u + 1}
      ⥤ Sheaf (topology W) RingCat.{u + 1})
    (adj : L ⊣ genericComponentRingPush W) (c : L.obj A ≅ B)
    [(SheafOfModules.pushforward.{u + 1}
      (adj.unit.app A ≫ (genericComponentRingPush W).map c.hom)).IsRightAdjoint]
    (E : Over (componentProfinite W)) [ExtremallyDisconnected E.left]
    (M : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} A) :
    Function.Bijective
      (((SheafOfModules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
        (adj.unit.app A ≫ (genericComponentRingPush W).map c.hom)).unit.app M).val.app
          (op E))
